sentences.text: Once upon a time, an old king became very sick.
His three sons felt great worry and pain in their hearts.
They loved their father very much, and they wanted to find a solution for his illness.
A wise man told them that the water of life could save the king.
If anyone drank this special water, he would get well immediately.
The oldest brother decided to go first on the journey to find the water.
He rode his horse along a mountain road until he met a small person.
The person asked him where he was going.
The proud brother answered with anger and rode away.
Soon, he fell into a narrow mountain pass and could not move forward.
He was stuck between the rocks and could not return home to his family.
After the first brother did not return, the second son started his own trip.
He also met the same person on the road and spoke to him very badly.
Because of his bad behavior, he also became stuck in a hidden place between the rocks.
The youngest brother, who was nice to everyone, finally left to seek the solution.
When the good young man met the person, he gave him some food and nice words.
The person, who was pleased by this royal behavior, told him where the special water was hidden.
He gave the boy a strong stick and a pair of bread pieces to open the ancient castle door.
The young royal followed these instructions carefully and entered the dark building without fear.
Inside the castle, he found the clear water of life and filled a small cup.
On his way back, he helped his two brothers escape from the mountain pass.
The three men traveled home together, bringing the wonderful solution to their sick father.
When the king drank the water, he stood up and lived happily for many years.
Every person in the country celebrated this event because the king was healthy again.
The family remained together for a long time, and peace covered the land.
The three brothers learned a valuable lesson about being good to everyone they met.
They understood that pride only brought trouble and failure.
Therefore, they always treated other people with respect and care.
The old king was proud of his youngest son, who had saved his life.
Years passed, but the story of the water of life was told again and again across the world.
Children grew up listening to this tale, learning that being good always wins in the end.
They knew that truth and love would always guide their actions through every difficult day.
The country remained safe, and people lived in peace for generations.
The memory of the good son stayed in the hearts of all who heard the story.
Long ago, the king had ruled his land with care and wisdom.
He always made sure that his people had food and support.
When he grew old and weak, his heart filled with worry.
He knew that his kingdom needed a strong leader for the future.
His three sons were supposed to protect the country after he died.
However, the older two sons were unkind and full of pride.
They only cared about money and power for themselves.
The youngest son was different because he always showed kindness to everyone.
He helped people who were poor or sick.
When the wise man spoke about the water of life, the king listened closely.
He hoped that his sons would learn an important lesson during their travels.
The journey was long and difficult for each brother.
Mountains stood tall against the sky, and roads were hard to follow.
The oldest brother rode fast because he wanted to find the water first.
He did not want to share the glory with anyone else.
When he met the small person on the mountain, he shouted at him.
The person became angry and used magic to trap him between the rocks.
The second brother made the exact same mistake.
He laughed at the little person and rode away quickly.
Soon, he was also trapped and unable to escape.
Both brothers learned that bad behavior leads to terrible problems.
Then the youngest son began his own trip.
Unlike his brothers, he stopped to talk to the small person.
He shared his bread and offered warm words of friendship.
The small person smiled and thanked the kind young man.
He told him where the castle was hidden in the dark forest.
The young man walked through the trees until he saw the ancient stone walls.
He used the stick and the bread pieces to open the heavy door.
Inside, the rooms were quiet and dark.
He found the water of life in a silver cup.
He filled his own bottle and started his journey back home.
On his way out of the castle, he found his brothers stuck in the pass.
They looked tired and very sad.
The youngest brother did not leave them behind.
He used his own strength to help them get out of the rocks.
The older brothers felt ashamed of how they had treated him before.
They walked together as a family and talked about their mistakes.
When they finally reached home, the king was waiting for them.
He drank the water and stood up immediately.
Everyone in the country cheered and clapped for joy.
The king hugged his youngest son and thanked him for saving his life.
From that day on, the brothers lived together in peace and happiness.

sentences.text: Long ago, an aged king ruled his prosperous realm with profound care and steady wisdom, ensuring his people always possessed food and support.
When he eventually grew old and weak, a heavy shadow of worry filled his heart, for he knew his kingdom needed a strong leader for the future.
His three sons were supposed to protect the country after he departed, yet the older two were unkind and consumed by arrogance.
They cared only about accumulating money and seizing personal power, while the youngest son remained remarkably different in spirit.
He consistently showed gentle kindness to everyone, readily helping people who were poor or suffering.
Then a terrible sickness befell the sovereign, and deep pain gripped the hearts of the royal brothers who loved their father dearly.
A wise counselor informed them that only the legendary water of life could reverse the monarch's fatal illness.
Whoever drank this miraculous liquid would recover his health immediately, defying even the grip of death.
When the wise man spoke about this cure, the anxious king listened closely, hoping his sons might learn an invaluable lesson during their travels.
Driven by a mixture of ambition and duty, the oldest brother decided to embark upon the perilous journey first.
The journey proved long and difficult for each brother, with towering mountains standing against the cold sky and treacherous roads.
The oldest son rode his horse rapidly along a winding mountain track, desperate to find the water before anyone else.
He had no intention of sharing the glory, marching forward with supreme confidence in his own superiority.
Along the way, he encountered a small person who politely asked where he was traveling.
The proud brother answered with biting anger, insulted that such a creature dared address him, and spurred his horse away.
Scarcely had he ridden another mile when he found himself trapped in a narrow mountain pass where the jagged rocks closed in around him.
Try as he might, he could move neither forward nor backward, completely stuck between the cold stones.
He could not return home to his family, paying a heavy price for his unyielding pride.
After the first brother failed to return, the second son started his own trip into the wild mountains.
He met the exact same small person on the narrow road and spoke to him with cruel disrespect.
Because of his arrogant behavior and sharp tongue, he suffered the exact same fate as his older sibling.
He was magically blocked in a hidden, desolate place between the rocks, unable to escape his stony prison.
Both arrogant brothers learned through bitter experience that bad behavior invariably leads to terrible problems.
They sat in isolation, regretting their foolish choices while the mountains watched in silent judgment.
Meanwhile, the youngest brother, who was inherently good-natured toward everyone, finally left to seek the salvation of their father.
Unlike his older brothers, the good young man paused when he met the small person on the mountain path.
He dismounted from his horse and greeted the traveler with warmth, willingly sharing his own food and offering kind words of friendship.
The small person was deeply pleased by this respectful, noble behavior and decided to aid the youth.
He revealed where the special water was hidden inside an ancient, forgotten castle deep within the dark forest.
To help him gain entry, the stranger gave the prince a sturdy stick and a pair of fresh bread pieces.
Armed with these unusual items, the young royal followed the precise instructions carefully and entered the dark forest without fear.
He walked beneath the towering trees until the ancient stone walls of the castle finally came into view.
Using the strong stick to steady his steps and the pieces of bread to appease the giant guardian doors, he opened the heavy entrance.
Inside the building, the vast rooms were quiet, shadowy, and filled with an eerie silence.
He navigated the empty halls bravely until he discovered the clear water of life gleaming in a silver cup.
Without hesitation, he filled his small bottle with the miraculous liquid and immediately began his journey back home.
On his way out of the ancient fortress, he discovered his two older brothers stuck fast in the narrow mountain pass.
They looked exhausted, starved, and profoundly ashamed as they stared at the ground.
The youngest brother did not abandon them to their fate, choosing mercy over resentment.
He used his own strength and the magical stick to help them dislodge the heavy rocks and regain their freedom.
Overwhelmed with gratitude and remorse, the older brothers felt deeply ashamed of how cruelly they had treated him in the past.
They walked together down the mountain as a reunited family, talking openly about their past mistakes and foolish pride.
When they finally reached home, the anxious king was waiting with dwindling strength for their return.
The moment the monarch drank the water of life, he stood up immediately, his vitality restored completely.
Every person in the entire country celebrated this joyous event, cheering and clapping in the streets because their beloved ruler was healthy once again.
The king hugged his youngest son tightly and thanked him repeatedly for saving his life.
From that day onward, the brothers lived together in peace, harmony, and mutual respect.
The three men had learned a profound lesson about treating everyone they met with genuine kindness.
They understood fully that arrogance brought only trouble and failure, whereas humility opened doors to success.
The old king remained endlessly proud of his youngest son, whose virtuous heart had preserved the kingdom.
Years passed, but the remarkable story of the water of life was told again and again across the entire world.
Generations of children grew up listening to this timeless tale, learning that goodness always triumphs in the end.
They understood that truth and love would reliably guide their actions through every difficult day they might face.
The country remained remarkably safe, and the people flourished in peace for decades to come.
The memory of the good son remained forever cherished in the hearts of all who heard the story.
